subject: EMEA demo variant: data residency + Private/VPC narrative + procurement pacing
body:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Simran Kaur <simran.kaur@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Dec 3, 2025 at 08:12 AM CET
Subject: EMEA demo variant: data residency + Private/VPC narrative + procurement pacing

Team — I’m seeing the same pattern across EMEA (esp. telecom + public sector-ish): they want to start with (1) data residency / retention controls, then (2) Private/VPC architecture, then they’re willing to hear economics/perf.

Can we lock an EMEA variant of the demo (deck + talk track) that:
- Leads with “Where does data go?” and “Who can access it?”
- Uses “Private (VPC) deployment” and “customer-managed networking + KMS” language (avoid anything that sounds like multi-tenant hosted)
- Sets expectations on procurement pacing (security review → DPA → SLA → final)

Concrete asks:
1) Soojin: can you propose a slide order / 3–5 bullets to add to the standard deck? Keep it tight enough for a 20–25 min exec audience.
2) Simran/Markus: what’s safe + real to show live vs what needs to be screenshots (e.g., residency controls, audit logs)?
3) Naomi: can you sanity-check our phrasing (residency vs sovereignty) so we don’t over-claim in the room?

Use case driving this: Summit Telecom (HubSpot record has “EU-only processing” and “no US support access” flagged).

Thanks,
Lukas
VP Sales, EMEA

Subject: Re: EMEA demo variant: data residency + Private/VPC narrative + procurement pacing

+1, this comes up constantly.

Summit (and two others last week) all asked variants of:
- “Is *any* prompt/response stored?”
- “Can you guarantee EU processing *and* EU support access?”
- “What’s the fastest path to a security sign-off?”

For the demo flow: I’d love a clean branch we can say out loud:

Option A (EMEA enterprise):
1) Security posture + residency + retention (2–3 mins)
2) Private/VPC architecture (5 mins, mostly narrative)
3) Console/audit logs (screenshots if needed)
4) Then do the API live bit (streaming + structured output)

Also procurement pacing: having a standard “what to expect” slide would be helpful, so it doesn’t feel like we’re inventing steps per customer.

Hannah

I can draft an EMEA-specific opening module we can slot into the existing deck without creating a forked “whole new deck.” Thinking:

Slide module (3 slides max):
1) “Deployment options + control boundaries”
   - Hosted API
   - Dedicated capacity
   - Private (VPC / on-prem)
   - Callout: same API + same operational tooling across modes

2) “Data handling + residency controls (what we do / what you control)”
   - Region pinning for inference execution
   - Configurable retention (incl. disable request/response storage)
   - Audit logs + access controls (RBAC/SSO)
   - Encryption and customer-managed keys for Private

3) “Procurement path (typical)”
   - Security review pack → DPA → SLA/terms → launch
   - What we can provide immediately (SOC2 letter, security FAQ links, architecture diagrams)

We should be careful on “EU-only support access” — we can say “restricted administrative access + audited access + access controls,” but Naomi should confirm the exact claim language.

I’ll send a first cut by EOD with speaker notes.

Soojin
Product Marketing

On what’s safe to show live:

Safe live (in demo tenant):
- Region selection for a route (show “EU (Frankfurt)” as the pinned execution region)
- Retention controls at a high level (toggle/setting names only; avoid clicking into any “raw logs” views during a call)
- RBAC roles view (coarse permissions only)

Prefer screenshots (to avoid demo brittleness / accidental exposure):
- Audit log event list (even though synthetic, it’s easy to derail the conversation)
- Private/VPC architecture diagram (we should control the framing)
- Any console views that might be empty if synthetic traffic lags

Also: Private/VPC story works best when we explicitly say “Customer-managed networking; we don’t require public ingress.” People relax when they hear that.

Markus: if you’re ok, I can send a cleaned-up diagram screenshot with callouts (control plane vs data plane, where the model execution happens, KMS/HSM).

Simran

Quick language guardrails (so we’re accurate and consistent):

Use:
- “Data residency / regional processing” (where inference execution occurs)
- “Region pinning” (customer-configured)
- “Configurable retention” and “option to disable storage of prompts/responses” (state as product capability; avoid implying this is default for all tenants)
- “Restricted administrative access, least privilege, and audited access”

Avoid:
- “EU-only support access” unless we qualify it (we can support regional support coverage, but making an absolute statement can trigger follow-up commitments we can’t universally guarantee across incidents)
- “Data sovereignty” unless we define it; most customers mean different things (legal jurisdiction, ownership, or staff location)

For procurement pacing slide: I like calling out what we can supply within 24 hours (SOC 2 report/letter, security FAQ, architecture diagram, DPA template) and what typically takes longer (pen test addenda, custom SLA carve-outs).

If Summit asks explicitly “Can any US-based employee access our data?” the correct answer is:
- “Access is controlled and logged; by design we minimize human access; for Private deployments, you control the network boundary and keys.”
(Then offer a follow-up with Security for the exact controls based on their deployment mode.)

Naomi
Security & Compliance Product Advisor
